Maria: FYI p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~130ms to ~420ms around 10:11 UTC; p50/p95 unchanged. Route view p99 reads ~180ms.

Josh: can you share the console query you ran?

Maria: ran: SELECT percentile(response_ms, [50,95,99]) FROM latency WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND timestamp >= '2024-05-05T10:05:00Z' AND timestamp <= '2024-05-05T10:20:00Z' GROUP BY route, sample_source

Kevin: heads-up: route rollups drop sample_source so route p99 is from mixed-origin t-digests. Endpoint page recomputes backend-only histograms after KV-cache filters. That can hide backend tails in route view.

Maria: that fits. endpoint/backend p99 ~430ms, route p99 ~180ms. Why would backend-only have a heavy tail but not show in route?

Liz: gateway and cache_hit samples dominate numerically and are low-latency. Route rollup gets overwhelmed by those. Backend had few samples but some long requests -> backend tail.

incident-bot: quota-fallback triggered client=acme-corp at 2024-05-05T10:11:07Z 12 routing -> fallback-model-v2.

Kevin: counts for window 10:05-10:20: gateway=1200, cache_hit=1020, backend=80. backend N is tiny.

Maria: proposal: expose sample_origin next to percentiles and show effective-N per-percentile. show low-confidence indicator when N < 100 to avoid noisy pages.

Liz: UX suggestion: small badge "origin: backend" or "origin: mixed" and tooltip with per-origin counts + effective N. red ! low-N indicator if N<100.

Josh: I'll file a tracking ticket and add runbook note: "When route p99 != endpoint p99, check sample_origin counts and effective N before paging SRE." Tagging eng-platform/oncall.

Kevin: I'll add metric percentile_effective_n in next infra deploy so console can consume it.

Liz: opened a tiny mock PR for badge/tooltip: https://git.internal/redwood/console/pull/5421. PTAL.

Maria: thanks all. tagging @eng-platform for visibility :eyes:
